Change: The Engineering Review plant lists (Plant / site, Preform plant, Blow plant, capacity-evidence Site) now offer Jim Zweifel's 22 locations, and Machine type offers his 14 types (EBM, IBM, ISBM, RHB, INJ - CAP, INJ - PREFORM, INJ - OTHER, DECO, PAD PRINTING, 12B, DIE CUTTING, LAMINATION, PRINTING, STAMPING). The placeholder plants and machine types are retired: quotes that have one keep it and show "(no longer offered)". Who the routing suggests for an engineer does not change.
Rationale: Jim sent QuoteFlow Plants and Process.xlsx on 2026-11-10 and Ben Whann confirmed it is correct, so it is loaded exactly as sent and marked approved (no check against the old "about 29"). Routing keys on the process type, not the machine type, so no mapping was needed. Filtering the plant list by machine type is suggested, not built. A read-only report lists quotes still on a retired value.

Change: Added the user-feedback build plan (FB-01 to FB-10), its prompts, the readiness split (build now / build with provisional config / wait for a decision) and this change log
Raised by: Feedback sessions Oct 26 to Nov 3; MVP User Feedback Review Nov 5
Rationale: The Nov 5 review agreed that Ben starts the clear MVP items and holds the ones blocked by open decisions. The plan groups items by the code they touch so each PR stays coherent and the number of CI waits stays low

Change: Once a gate is approved, its section is read-only for everyone: the engineering review and capacity (after G2), the pricing record and capital readiness (after G3), and the commercial terms and capital flag (after G4 Advance). The screen says "Locked after G2 · decided by … on … · reopens if the quote is sent back" and the server refuses any change (409). A send-back (Pricing → Engineering or → KAM, Final Review return, customer re-quote) reopens the section it goes back to and every later one.
Rationale: Pricing saw terms, engineering and pricing fields stay editable after approval (Oct 30); the tracker's acceptance is "after a gate is approved, its sections are read-only for all roles except via send-back". Engineering and pricing were already limited to their own stage; the real gap was the terms and capital flag, editable until close. Built as one rule per section in the domain (it reads the decision history and the configured stage order, so it follows any change to the stages) and enforced on every write route, because the UI is never the control (CLAUDE.md rule 1). Roles that may not edit a section at all keep their 403; every role that may gets 409. Terms stay editable during Final Review so the KAM can still check them; locking them at final review approval with the approver finalizing them (F-068) waits on D-003 (FB-08). Refused attempts are not audited, matching every other refusal.

Change: Pricing can send a quote back to the KAM ("Rework (back to KAM)" at G3) with a reason and a required note, next to the existing "Rework (back to Engineering)". Only the pricing lead decides it, like every G3 decision. The KAM is told in-app and by email and sees it under "Returned to me" with the reason and note.
Rationale: Kyle asked in the Pricing walkthrough (Oct 30) for a way to kick a quote back to the KAM; only "back to Engineering" existed (Q-010). Built as a new G3 outcome in the workflow config (reason from the rework list, note required, version bump like every rework) and shipped to existing environments by a data migration, so it is config, not code (CLAUDE.md rule 4). It goes through lead review like the other G3 outcomes: a pricer submits to the pricing lead, who decides (L-9). The label, help text and reason list are provisional until Pricing confirms them. Also fixed the KAM dashboard's "Returned to me", which only listed G1 / G2 returns.

Change: When the KAM resubmits a quote Pricing sent back, they answer "Did the scope change?" (product, volume, resin, drawing or plant). No: it goes straight back to Quoting with the same pricer and pricing lead, and the pricer can edit again. Yes: it is routed as a new submission (qualification if switched on, then Engineering). The answer is on the timeline and in the audit log.
Rationale: Kyle's point (Oct 30): a KAM fixing a commercial detail should not send the quote through Engineering again; the tracker's acceptance is "goes back directly to Pricing unless scope change is flagged". Built as an outcome setting (resume at origin or at intake), seeded "origin" only for the new G3 send-back, so G1 and G2 reworks behave exactly as before. The quote remembers where the rework came from until it is resubmitted. The question is required so nobody skips Engineering by accident. Because a rework creates a new quote version, Pricing records the price approval again on the new version (the earlier one stays on record, CR-38). The scope-change wording is provisional.

Change: The Final Review approver is no longer blocked by fields other roles own. Whether the terms check and the Legal review block release is now a setting (g4_required_checks), set to block neither. The review screen shows the terms and the Legal review read-only, and lists an open check as a warning with a link to the quote's Commercial panel; the decision records that the approver saw the warnings.
Raised by: Ben Whann (Build team), seen in the Sales & Marketing leadership demo (Nov 3)
Rationale: In the Nov 3 demo the approver could not release the offer until a sales leader ticked "terms checked", and the Legal review acted as required, though neither is the approver's field and neither was on the review screen. The tracker's acceptance: "approver can complete final review without fields owned by other roles; legal review is optional." Who finalizes terms is still open (D-003, built in FB-08), so the rule is config, not a hard-coded change: g4_required_checks is seeded [] (provisional) and an Admin can switch either check back on without a release. Open checks stay visible as warnings so nothing is approved blind. A malformed setting fails closed (both block).

Change: A note is now required for every exception decision at every gate: Advance with risk, Capital required, Hold, Rework (including re-cost, return and re-quote), Redirect and Stop. A plain Advance, Approve or Awarded still needs none. The decision dialog marks the note "Required for exception decisions".
Rationale: Agreed in the Pricing walkthrough (Oct 30) and decided as D-015: minimise free text, and keep notes for exceptions and escalations. Built in the outcome configuration (requires_note) and carried to test and production by a data migration, since the seed alone does not change rows an admin has touched. 11 more outcomes now need a note (25 in all). Rows stay provisional until Bailey approves the list. Text caps are not part of this (D-016, FB-09).

Change: Verified, no change needed: when an engineer or pricer submits their work, every engineering lead (or pricing lead) gets an in-app notice and an email. Integration tests now cover it.
Rationale: Built under L-9 (Oct 30) and marked in progress in the tracker. FB-01 adds the test the tracker's scenario describes (every EngLead gets the in-app row and the email) instead of rebuilding it. It passed on the first run. Who the engineering lead is and who signs capacity remain D-008 (FB-06).

Change: Verified, no change needed: the pricing lead assigns a quote to a pricer, the pricer is told in-app and by email, and finds it under their assignments in the pricing queue. Integration tests now cover it.
Rationale: Built in B-26 (A6) and marked in progress in the tracker. FB-01 adds the scenario test; it passed on the first run.

Change: Verified, no change needed: a pricer submits completed pricing to the pricing lead, who is told and either approves it (G3) or sends it back with a required note; the pricer can then edit again. Integration tests now cover it.
Rationale: Built under L-9 (Oct 30): the pricer submits to the lead and only the pricing lead decides G3. FB-01 adds the scenario test (approve and send-back paths); it passed on the first run.

Change: Capacity evidence now shows each line's utilization before the new business (typed) and after it (calculated and read-only, from cavitation, cycle time, effectiveness, run days and the volume given to that line). "Buffer %" is gone. When the quote is split across lines or plants, each row carries its own share and the screen warns, without blocking, if the shares do not add up to the quote's volume. Over 100 % shows red "exceeds line capacity", over 85 % amber, and the basis is stated under the table
Raised by: Paul Slomkowski, Faron Ipox (Engineering; Supply Chain)
Rationale: Engineering and Supply Chain (Nov 3) said three people defined "buffer" three ways and asked for utilization before and after, calculated. The formula is the shape of Faron Ipox's Nov 4 email with the OEE applied once: his step 2 names it twice, almost certainly a typo that A-023 asks him to confirm. The stored figure is calculated by the server and re-derived if the cavitation changes, so it cannot drift. The buffer and old utilization columns are kept (deprecated) for history and Fabric; old utilization values moved into "before". Not done: a choice of utilization basis (F-060, P1) and deriving trending OEE from 4- and 13-month averages. Provisional, awaiting D-021: 350 run days a year, amber above 85 %, basis label "Trailing 12 months actual, trending OEE (provisional, D-021)" (setting `capacity_basis`, an Admin can change it)

Change: Capacity evidence can be downloaded as a CSV (every row with its calculated after-utilization, the basis, the quote number and when it was made) and a capacity analysis file can be attached from the same section
Raised by: Faron Ipox, Bailey Schmitt (Supply Chain; PMO)
Rationale: Supply Chain wanted the evidence to support a later CER without asking for the data again. The download is audited as an export and uses the same access as the Engineering tab. Attachments get a new "Capacity analysis" kind. The tracker also says the capacity section must be filled in before Engineering advances: that is already enforced by the G2 rules (at least one capacity row and the capacity sign-off), so no new rule was added

Change: Engineering's capital figure is now called "Budgetary capital estimate (USD): preliminary, includes contingency" everywhere it is shown (Engineering, Quoting, Final Review, the quote list and its export). The CER reference box is gone from Quoting (an old value still shows, read-only, as "Legacy CER reference"). Capital status labels now say "(budgetary)", for example "Capital pre-approved (budgetary)". Commit & Hand Off has a "Ready for CER development" tick, available only after the award, recording who and when
Rationale: Engineering said "we've been burned way too many times" by a budgetary quote reading as CER-ready. The CER is built after award, so the tick lives on the hand-off record where only the people who can edit it use it, and the server refuses it before the award. Status codes and the G3 rules are unchanged because the capital-readiness structure is part of D-001 (FB-07). The old CER reference column is kept for history

Change: The EBM wheel can no longer be picked as a machine type (quotes that already have it still show it), and cavitation accepts whole numbers from 1 to 99 only. The plant list is unchanged
Rationale: Engineering confirmed both fixes. The database check on cavitation is added "not validated" so rows already saved are not rejected (none exist in the seed data; on a live environment, check `eng_review` for values over 99, which could not be re-saved until corrected). The plant list waits for Jim Zweifel's active plant list (FB-09)

Change: The Engineering review shows the intake's product facts at the top. Today that is the resin; the customer-specified grade, PCR %, colour, additives and the variants note appear when the intake overhaul (FB-02) merges
Raised by: Kyle Arnold, Tania Nazario (Pricing; Sales and Marketing leadership)
Rationale: Pricing and Sales leadership said material, colour and additives drive cost and must reach Engineering. Only the resin exists in the app until FB-02 adds the other fields, so the header renders a list from the server and FB-02 adds entries without changing the screen

Change: No new-customer form. The customer is always the Salesforce Account on the picked opportunity, shown read-only with a "from Salesforce" tag. The KAM answers one question: "Not yet a Pretium customer (no ERP account)", which still triggers the new-customer Legal review. An opportunity with no Account can't be submitted; the KAM adds the Account in Salesforce first.
Raised by: John Kraus, Jordan Albin, Amanda Cronkhite (KAM)
Rationale: KAMs said new accounts start in Salesforce (account request form) and there is no ERP setup until the business is won (D-011, Nov 2). So QuoteFlow stops collecting customer name, location and contact and takes the SF Account as the customer; the "not yet a customer" checkbox keeps DEC-27 / CLAUDE.md rule 7 and the Legal trigger. The old typed columns are kept (deprecated, not written) so existing quotes keep their history. Nothing is created in Salesforce or the ERP (no write-back in MVP). T-004 needs no code: a prospect created in Salesforce shows in the picker after the next sync.

Change: No double entry: what Salesforce already holds pre-fills and is read-only with a "from Salesforce" tag (resin, neck, volume and container size from the product spec). Revenue and the ship / fill destination stay editable (the destination with a reason, as before). The Salesforce close date is shown read-only from the latest sync and labelled "updates with Salesforce"; QuoteFlow no longer stores its own close date.
Rationale: KAMs re-typed opportunity data and the close date didn't come through. T-009 asked whether the close date is a snapshot or live: it is now read from the latest synced opportunity everywhere (intake, quote, pipeline filters and sort), so there is one close date, Salesforce's. The stored expected_close_date is deprecated (kept for history and analytics, not written). Read-only is enforced in the wizard; the server doesn't re-read Salesforce at submit (the KAM corrects Salesforce and re-picks the opportunity).

Change: Two required dates replace the editable close date: "Quote needed by" (after today) and "Product needed by" (best estimate of launch need, on or after Quote needed by). Quote needed by now drives the timing part of the priority score.
Rationale: KAMs said the quote-needed date, not the SF close date, is what Engineering should prioritise on. The scoring engine gets a new model version (v2) whose timing attribute reads Quote needed by; weights and bands are unchanged because D-004 is open, and earlier scores keep their version. "Today" is judged in US Central. Both dates are in the intake required-field setting and in the INTAKE_COMPLETE rule (data migration), so quotes submitted earlier and still waiting at G1 need them added (Rework to the KAM) before G1 Advance. Values provisional.

Change: The neck is three pick-lists from Jim Zweifel's standard list: neck diameter (13–155 mm, 409, 605D), neck finish (400, 410, 415, 485, CRC, BeriCap, DBJ, Deep Skirt, J-Cap, Jigger, Kerr, Pano, PCO-1810, PCO-1881, Ratchet, ROPP, Snap) and an optional special feature (CT, Multi Lead, Tamper Evident, Vented). "Other" is now "Custom" and needs a short description. Existing quotes and open drafts were converted (e.g. 28-410 → 28 + 410).
Raised by: Jordan Albin, John Kraus (KAM); Faron Ipox (Supply Chain); Jim Zweifel (Engineering)
Rationale: KAMs and Engineering agreed to split the neck and use Engineering's standard list; Engineering asked for "Custom" with a description instead of "Other" (T-020). Deviation: the tracker says two fields, Jim's later list (Field Inventory, Nov 5) has three, so three were built. The migration splits 28-410 / 38-400 / 89-400 / 110-400, turns 120 DC into 120 + Custom "DC" and keeps any other text as a Custom finish. The Salesforce Neck_Finish__c pre-fill uses the same rule and stays blank when it can't be read. The old list is deactivated, not deleted. All three lists are provisional until Jim signs them off (F-020).

Change: A "Customer-specified resin" checkbox reveals a required "Supplier / grade" (e.g. LyondellBasell Pro-fax 6331). It is shown to Engineering and Pricing on the quote, the Engineering tab and Final Review.
Rationale: Pricing needs the exact material when the customer dictates it, not just "polypropylene". A checkbox plus one short field (≤ 120) keeps free text minimal (D-015); the grade is cleared if the box is unticked. Visible to every role that reads the quote (CLAUDE.md rule 2), which covers Engineering and Pricing (T-013).

Change: Components: Decoration added. Picking a component shows its follow-up questions, required while it is picked and cleared when it isn't: Liner → liner spec; Label → labels purchased by (Customer / Pretium); Decoration → decoration type (Silk screen, Hot stamp, Shrink sleeve, Other) and number of print colors (1–12).
Rationale: KAMs asked for the details Engineering and Pricing chase for each component. Which component asks which question is kept in the component list's configuration (not code), because Bailey noted Pretium's component list isn't final (V-090). Decoration, the label-buyer and decoration-type lists are provisional.

Change: New attachment kinds: Bid file, Project brief and Competitor / incumbent drawing. An optional "Customer RFP / portal link" (https only) is captured and shown to every role that reads the quote. Files whose names contain commas, ampersands or slashes (e.g. "P&G, bottle 1/2 rev.pdf") now upload with their full name and open for Engineering.
Raised by: Jordan Albin, Jeff Curry (KAM); Jim Zweifel (Engineering)
Rationale: Agreed in the KAM and Engineering sessions. T-003 found a real defect: the upload parser cut a name at the last "/" ("P&G, bottle 1/2 rev.pdf" became "2 rev.pdf"). The full name is now kept for display and download, and the stored file name swaps "/" for "_" so SharePoint accepts it. A competitor drawing counts as a drawing for F-016. The RFP link is limited to https links so it can't point anywhere unsafe.

Change: "Modify an existing mold" checkbox: reveals the existing mold / part number and what changes (e.g. finish change 28-410 → 28-400), with a prompt to attach the reference drawing or a part photo. The Engineering queue shows a "Mold modification" chip.
Rationale: PMO confirmed mold modifications are in scope when capital or engineering review is needed. Two short required fields (≤ 60 and ≤ 500) keep it structured; the drawing or photo goes in as an attachment. The chip lets the Engineering lead see it in the queue (T-012).

Change: A quote can be submitted only with a bottle or competitor drawing attached, or every field of the minimum spec filled: height, width or diameter, depth, gram weight (new fields, mm and g), neck (diameter and finish), resin and color. The wizard shows which path is met and names what's missing; a drawing status of Coming / Sample only / None no longer submits on its own.
Raised by: John Kraus (KAM); Paul Slomkowski, Jim Zweifel (Engineering); Matthew Graden, Tania Nazario (Sales/Marketing Leadership)
Rationale: Engineering can't quote without a drawing or the minimum specs (D-018, decided Nov 3). The rule is in the domain and enforced by the API (422 DRAWING_OR_MIN_SPEC_REQUIRED, listing the missing fields) and the wizard. The list is the setting intake_min_spec_fields, seeded provisionally from D-018, so Jim Zweifel / Danielle Leu can change it without a release; A-024's layer structure and container photo would need new fields first and are not added. Without a drawing the quote still shows the "takes longer" note.

Change: "Ship / fill destination": city and state are required, pre-filled from the Salesforce Account's shipping address, and shown on the Engineering queue and the Engineering tab.
Rationale: Engineering decides the plant with the KAM's input on destination and logistics (D-012). The Account shipping address is the pre-fill today; the opportunity's free-text Ship_to_Locations__c isn't mapped yet (TODO D-18). City and state replace the old street-or-city rule in the required-field setting (data migration).

Change: Color (Natural or Custom color with a short description) and an optional additives note at intake, shown to Engineering and Pricing.
Rationale: Color and additives are cost drivers Pricing and Engineering need at hand-off. A two-value list plus short text keeps free text small; the color list is provisional. They show on the quote, in the Engineering tab's "From intake" header and on Final Review (FB-03 adds them to its Engineering review header).

Change: PCR % in the resin section, from the standard levels 0, 25, 50 and 100%.
Raised by: Faron Ipox (Supply Chain); Jim Zweifel, Paul Slomkowski (Engineering)
Rationale: Engineering and Supply Chain agreed standard levels instead of custom percentages, as a starting point; the list is provisional config. The existing PCR-HDPE / PCR-PET resin codes are kept and not migrated.

Change: Only CCQ requests can be submitted. Choosing stock, stock-plus, a price inquiry or other capital shows: "Stock, stock-plus, price inquiries and pack-out evaluations stay in the pricing application for now. Submit them there." and Submit stays disabled.
Rationale: For MVP the pricing application stays in use for non-CCQ work. The allowed classes and the message are settings (provisional), so D-030 can change where pack-out changes go without a release. The server refuses another class with 422 REQUEST_CLASS_NOT_ALLOWED. G1 Redirect remains for CCQ requests that turn out not to be CCQ work.

Change: Optional "Quote variants requested" note (up to 300 characters), e.g. "price at 0/25/50% PCR; near-site vs ideal-site", shown to Engineering and Pricing.
Raised by: Danielle Leu (Engineering); Faron Ipox (Supply Chain); Jordan Albin (KAM)
Rationale: The interim answer to D-017 (option B): Engineering and Pricing see the ask without any data-model branching. Structured multi-scenario quotes stay in F-056 (P1). The limit is a provisional setting.

Change: Only sales leaders can override a quote's priority tier, and they must give a reason of at least 15 characters. KAMs, Engineering leads and Pricing no longer see an override option; KAMs see "Need a different priority? Escalate to your sales leader.". The sales leader's reason shows on the Engineering queue row and under "Why this priority?" on the quote.
Raised by: Sales & Marketing leadership (Matthew Graden, Tania Nazario, Jennifer Wulf); decided with Bailey Schmitt (PMO), Nov 3
Rationale: Sales leadership and the PMO decided priority should be a sales call, with the reason passed to Engineering (D-028, Nov 3). The override is self-applied and logged (like ship-to), so a leader's decision takes effect at once; it can be reverted in one click. The setting is changed by a data migration. A request a KAM, Engineering lead or Pricer raised before the change is not auto-rejected: it stays open for a sales leader to approve or reject. Queue position and ship-to are unchanged. The KAM path is the existing escalation. Tracker note: confirm with KAMs before the pilot (D-028).

Change: Checked that the priority score is calculated correctly: five representative quotes were scored by hand and the engine matches every one (strong and weak revenue, volume, timing and capital, plus band edges and unknown capital). No defect was found. Weights and bands are unchanged.
Raised by: KAM and Sales & Marketing leadership feedback (tracker bug F-005)
Rationale: The tracker said the score might be off; it was recomputed by hand from the scoring model, with the working shown in a test, against both the original model and the one that reads "Quote needed by". Everything agreed, so no code fix was needed; the test now guards the calculation. Not done: changing weights, bands or tiers, which wait for D-004 (FB-10).

Change: The "Why this priority?" panel shows the quote's market and the strategic-fit points it contributed, marked "provisional" while no points are set. The scoring settings can now hold a segment-level map next to the market map; a segment wins over a market, then the default.
Rationale: Melanie's Where-to-Play 9-box is by segment, but QuoteFlow's market list is coarse and the placement of segments in cells is unconfirmed, so no points are seeded: every quote still scores a neutral 50 and the panel says so. Building the mechanism now means FB-10 only loads data once D-004 chooses segment vs market and the points per cell. Tests use a made-up map to prove two markets, and two segments, score differently.

Change: "$0 CER" is now "$0 CER (customer-reimbursed capital)" with an ⓘ explaining it, and a new funding option "Shared (company and customer)" is available.
Feedback IDs: F-022; V-055; follows D-023; D-003 open
Rationale: Oleg defined $0 CER on Nov 3: it follows the standard quoting process and the customer reimburses the capital; his wording is the help text, with no separate workflow path. Jennifer asked for "Shared"; it is provisional until D-003 decides the terms structure, and its help text says to record the split in the terms notes. Both are value-list changes delivered by a data migration.

Change: The quote header shows "Open in Salesforce ↗" (new tab) once an Admin sets the Salesforce URL, and the plain opportunity ID until then. After a customer outcome is recorded, a dismissible reminder says "Update the Salesforce opportunity to match: <stage>" with the link.
Rationale: Salesforce write-back is deferred (D-014, F-035), so this is the stopgap: a link and a prompt, with nothing written to Salesforce. The instance URL is a setting seeded empty (the existing Salesforce connection only knows a login URL, so it is not reused). The stage named comes from a small provisional setting (awarded → Verbal Award, negotiating → Negotiating, lost and expired → Closed Lost, re-quote → Quoting) because several Salesforce stages share one CCQ stage; KAMs should confirm it. The existing Salesforce mismatch flag still works.

Change: When a gate decision moves a quote forward (qualify, engineering, pricing, Final Review, the customer's award), the next owner and the KAM are told, in-app and by email with a link. Engineering leads, backup assigners and the assigned engineer hear a quote is ready for engineering; the pricing lead and pricers hear it is ready for pricing; the approvers hear it is ready for Final Review; the KAM hears "moved on to <stage>". The person who made the decision is not told, and a person who holds two of these roles gets one notice, not two.
Raised by: John Kraus (KAM); Jim Zweifel (Engineering); Jennifer Wulf (Sales/Marketing Leadership)
Rationale: KAMs said "once submitted, we don't know where it stands"; Engineering asked for automatic notice to everyone when work is ready for hand-off. The outcomes already declared who to notify but the app only logged it, so those targets are now delivered and the next owner and KAM are added on top. One resolver in the domain (not a message per screen) so every gate and any admin-configured outcome behaves the same, and one notification per person per event. The email never carries notes or figures. Not done: due dates (F-072, waiting on D-020). D-010 (interaction model) is still open; it informed the design but did not block it. The KAM now gets an email on every advance; it can be switched off per type in preferences.

Change: Every send-back now says so in plain words. The KAM is told "returned to you" with who sent it back, the reason and the note (in-app; the email has the reason, not the note), for qualification, engineering and the new Pricing "back to KAM". A quote sent back to Engineering from Pricing says "returned from Pricing" (and "back with you" for the engineer), not "new"; Final Review returns, customer re-quotes, re-quotes at Commit & Hand Off and a pricing re-cost tell the assigned person and the lead, and the KAM sees it was sent back. After a KAM fixes a Pricing send-back with no scope change, the assigned pricer and the pricing lead are told "back from the KAM".
Raised by: John Kraus (KAM); Kyle Arnold (Pricing); Jim Zweifel (Engineering)
Rationale: FB-01 added the G3 to KAM loop but only the KAM's own notice existed; Pricing and Engineering had no way to know a quote was back. Returns reuse the existing arrival notices with a "returned from" line so nobody is told twice. The lead is told as well as the assignee (the prompt said assignee only) because the lead decides the gate and the resubmission rule names both. Not done: the note text in any email (existing privacy rule).

Change: Holds and closures reach the right people. A hold tells the hold owner ("you own the hold") and the KAM, with the review date. Stop, Redirect, Decline, Lost, Expired, Commitment not authorized and Won tell the KAM; a Final Review decline also still tells Pricing and the price approver.
Rationale: The outcome config already said "tell the KAM" on a closure but nothing was delivered. Closures email at once rather than as a daily digest: the digest machinery builds only the 7 AM "to qualify" list, and a closure the KAM did not cause is worth knowing now. A closures digest can follow if it proves noisy.

Change: When an engineer or pricer submits to their lead, the KAM now sees it reached the lead, and when the lead sends it back the KAM sees that too (in-app only, no email). The lead, the engineer and the pricer notices are unchanged.
Rationale: The KAM could not see where a quote sat inside Engineering or Pricing. In-app only because those steps are internal and frequent. Engineers and pricers are still told when the lead sends their work back, and the lead when work is submitted.

Change: A comment on a quote now notifies the quote's KAM, the assigned engineer (in Engineering) or pricer (in Quoting), the stage lead and everyone who commented before, in-app and by email with a link. The author is not told, and someone who is @mentioned gets the mention instead. The email says "3 new comments on CCQ-…" and links to them; it never repeats the comment. Several comments within 10 minutes arrive as one email.
Rationale: KAMs asked to be alerted when someone comments or requests something on a quote. The comment text is never emailed (the comment may mention prices). The 10 minute window is a provisional setting (comment_email_collapse_minutes, 0 sends each at once) because nobody has said how many emails is too many. The Final Review approvers are included as the stage lead (not in the prompt). Not done: a separate "request" action; D-010 is open and a comment is the only request channel for now.

Change: Verified again after the change: an engineer submitting tells every engineering lead in-app and by email (T-014), an engineer's or pricer's submission and the lead's decision or send-back tell the next owner, the assignee and the KAM (T-037), and a KAM's comment reaches the assigned engineer (T-010). Integration tests cover all three.
Rationale: F-003 was already working (FB-01 verified it); this re-check makes sure the new delivery did not double or drop a notice. Not done: nothing was found to fix.

Change: Recorded the decisions from three meetings: D-001 decided (costing, then ROI, then price confirmation as steps inside Quoting), D-031 (the gate is called "Price approved"), D-032 (what the KAM captures at intake about payment, funding, dunnage and freight) and D-033 (the equipment BOM is an upload of the one-page CSR BOM). Change: Costing, ROI and price approval are now three steps inside Quoting, in order. 1) Pricing uploads the costing model (one workbook: costs and the initial price assumptions) and ticks "Costing completed", which now needs the model on file. 2) When capital is required ($0 CER included), Finance uploads the ROI model; otherwise the step says "Not required" and why. 3) The pricing lead approves the price (G3), optionally with an updated price table. The pricing lead cannot approve the price until the costing model and, when needed, the ROI model are on file. Each step shows who did it and when, on the Quoting tab and at Final Review; Finance is told when the costing model is ready, the pricing lead when the ROI is in.
Raised by: Gemma Cebolla (Pricing); decided by Bailey Schmitt (PMO), Gemma Cebolla (Pricing) and Stacy Slocum (Finance) with Oleg Yarovinski (Sponsor)
Rationale: Gemma: "it's kind of weird to approve a price without knowing what my ROI is" (V-018). D-001 (Nov 9) replaced the earlier ask (a separate costing gate, then pricing and ROI in parallel) with costing, then ROI, then price confirmation as steps inside Quoting, not a gate and not in parallel; the build follows it, so the tracker's F-032 text should be updated (tracker-updates-2026-11-09.md). Built like lead review: parts of a stage, enforced by the G3 rules (current costing model; ROI model when required), so no new stage, gate or analytics break. When the ROI is required is config (roi_required_when, provisional: G2 "capital required", the capital-likely flag, or a customer-funded / $0 CER funding model; "Shared" not included) for Stacy and Gemma to confirm. Finance is an input, not an approver. Not done: a notice to Finance when a quote becomes ROI-required after its costing model was uploaded. A-036 (Oleg confirming D-001 in writing) is still open.

Change: Re-uploading a costing model (or ROI model, or price table) keeps one record per quote with its history: the new file becomes version 2 and is flagged current, earlier versions stay listed and downloadable, and no duplicate attachments pile up. Removing a wrong upload (within 24 hours) makes the previous version current again.
Rationale: Gemma: every change to the costing workbook meant deleting or re-uploading another copy (synthesis E3). Built as general, kind-scoped versioning on attachments (version, superseded_by, superseded_at; one current version per quote and kind enforced by the database), used for the three Quoting models; other file kinds stay a simple list. Uploads, the supersede and restores are audited and on the timeline. Version numbers never repeat. T-034 is ready to test.

Change: Intake step 3 now asks what payment terms the customer is requesting (Net 15, 30, 45, 60, 90, 120 or Other with a short description) and whether the customer pays for any of the tooling or capital (the funding list, plus a new "Not discussed" that it starts on). Choosing a customer-funded, shared, $0 CER or amortized answer shows a one-line hint that a customer-owned tool has sales-tax and contract implications. The amount and how it is paid are not asked here.
Raised by: Gemma Cebolla (Pricing), Kyle Arnold (Pricing), Cait Catanzaro (Pricing); decided by Gemma Cebolla and Bailey Schmitt on 2026-11-06
Rationale: Pricing needs the customer's requested payment terms for awareness and negotiation: a longer term (Net 60, Net 120) costs Pretium borrowing, but it does not change the costing. Payment terms and tooling funding are two separate things (D-032), so intake asks only the funding question that decides whether Pricing and Tax need to look (whether the customer pays for any tooling), and leaves the amount and payment method (upfront, 50/50, per piece) to the terms in FB-08. The requested terms are stored on the intake, not on the terms record, so FB-08 can reconcile them. Whether a request is non-standard is read from a setting (standard_payment_terms: Net 15 and Net 30, decided Nov 9, still marked provisional until an Admin approves it), so it changes without a rebuild. It does not set the "non-standard terms" Legal trigger. Everything is optional: a blank shows as a warning, not a block (D-006 is open). The "Not discussed" value, the other list values and the help text are provisional.
